newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: DMCI says plans $250 mln cement plant.
newsitem.headline: DMCI says plans $250 mln cement plant.

text.p: Construction firm DMCI Holdings Inc plans to build a $250 million cement plant in Semirara island in the central Philippines, President Isidro Consunji told analysts at a briefing on Tuesday.
Consunji also said his company is set to sign a six-billion peso construction contract with Rockwell Land Corp, a unit of Benpres Holdings Corp, by the end of this month.
"We are looking for a partner now (for the cement plan)," Consunji said.
DMCI has had preliminary talks with Marubeni Corp and Itochu Corp for a possible joint venture on the project but nothing definite had come out of the talks, he said.

Last month, DMCI said its board approved the purchase of 40 percent of Semirara Coal Corp held by Voest Alpine Machinery Construction and Engineering Gmbh, a unit of VA Technologies AG, for 905 million pesos.
Consunji also said DMCI would put up five high-rise towers in the Rockwell property in Manila's Makati commercial centre.
The project, to be undertaken in a joint venture with a British partner, will be completed in 30 months, he said.
Rockwell plans to convert a 15.5 hectare of prime land owned by Manila Electric Co into a mix-used commercial and residential centre.
